chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man whose wealth is absent for five years, then he comes to it and the principal wealth is not returned to him; how much should he pay zakat on it? He said: 'One year.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And there is no zakat on debt unless its delay is from the side of the owner himself. That to which this points is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: How much zakat is due on wealth that was absent for five years and then returned?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the specific case of absent wealth (*mal al-gha'ib*), establishing that only one year of zakat is due upon recovery if the principal remains intact. The accompanying commentary by al-Tusi distinguishes this from debt (*dayn*), clarifying that zakat is not levied on owed amounts unless the delay is due to the debtor's retention, a nuance critical for understanding liquidity in Shia jurisprudence.
